data.case_title: Suspicious "refund" letter demanding an upfront fee (likely scam)
data.title: "Your refund of €612.00 has been approved" – advance-fee request
data.summary: A letter from an entity calling itself "Verbraucher-Rückerstattungsstelle Energie", based in Nicosia, Cyprus, claims the recipient is owed a €612.00 refund from energy bills 2023–2025, but demands a €49.90 "processing fee" be paid first, by 27 November 2026, to a Cypriot IBAN. This matches the classic pattern of an advance-fee scam.
data.explanation: This letter shows strong signs of being a scam (Betrug): it uses obviously placeholder-style names and addresses ("Beispielacker", "Mustermünster", "Avenue Beispiel"), it is sent from a foreign (Cypriot) address for a supposedly German consumer matter, and it asks you to pay a fee upfront before you can receive a promised "refund" — real German authorities or energy providers never require you to pay a fee to receive money owed to you. Do not transfer any money to the given account. Do not reply with personal or bank details. If you want to be safe, you can report this letter to the police (Polizei) or your consumer protection center (Verbraucherzentrale) and simply ignore the deadline.

warnings: This document shows strong signs of being an advance-fee scam: it asks for an upfront fee before paying out a promised refund, a pattern never used by legitimate German authorities or energy providers.

The sender's address is in Nicosia, Cyprus, yet the letter concerns a German consumer energy-cost refund, and the recipient's address ('Mustermünster') and name ('Beispielacker') look like placeholder/example text rather than real details.
The payment IBAN (CY17...) is a foreign account; sending money there is unlikely to ever be recoverable.
Do not reply to the given email/phone or send any personal, banking or ID information to this sender.
